_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Indigenous Peoples of Togo
910.label: Event
910.description: Early settlement of the Togo hills; Ewe, Kabye, Tem, and other peoples establish diverse societies.

910.name: Early Settlement and Koutammakou
910.label: Event
910.description: Archaeological evidence of early habitation; Koutammakou region of Batammariba people; fortified tower-houses (takienta).

910.name: Ewe, Kabye, and Tem Peoples
910.label: Event
910.description: Ewe migrations from Notsie; Kabye highland farming communities; Tem traders link forest and savanna.

920.name: Migrations and Early State Formation
920.label: Event
920.description: Ewe migration from Notsie; Dagomba and other northern influence; decentralised political systems.

920.name: Ewe Migration from Notsie
920.label: Event
920.description: Ewe oral tradition recounts exodus from Notsie under tyrannical king Agokoli; dispersal across southern Togo and Ghana.

920.name: Northern Kingdoms and Dagomba Influence
920.label: Event
920.description: Dagomba, Tchokossi, and Bassar polities in northern Togo; iron smelting at Bassar; trans-regional trade.

930.name: Slave Coast Trade and Togo
930.label: Event
930.description: Southern Togo as part of the Slave Coast; Aneho (Little Popo) and Agoué as trading centres; Danish, Dutch, and Portuguese factors.

930.name: Little Popo (Aneho) Slave Trade
930.label: Event
930.description: Aneho as major slave-trading port; Mina and other groups mediate between European traders and interior.

930.name: Coastal Commerce and European Presence
930.label: Event
930.description: Danish, Dutch, Portuguese, and later German traders; palm oil replaces slave trade; Agoué and coastal settlements.

940.name: German Togoland
940.label: Event
940.description: Gustav Nachtigal secures protectorate 1884; Musterkolonie (model colony); railway and cocoa; WWI conquest.

940.name: Nachtigal Treaty and German Protectorate
940.label: Event
940.description: Gustav Nachtigal signs treaty with chief Mlapa III at Togoville 1884; Berlin Conference confirms German claim.

940.name: Musterkolonie (Model Colony)
940.label: Event
940.description: Germans develop Togoland as showcase colony; railways, cocoa plantations, Lomé port; relatively less violent than other colonies.

940.name: French Mandate and Trust Territory
940.label: Event
940.description: League of Nations mandate then UN Trust Territory under France; Ewe unification movement; path to independence.

940.name: French Mandate Administration
940.label: Event
940.description: France administers eastern two-thirds of former Togoland; forced labour; cocoa and coffee economy.

940.name: Ewe Unification Movement
940.label: Event
940.description: All-Ewe Conference demands reunification of Ewe people split between French Togo and British Gold Coast; UN plebiscites.

950.name: Independence and Sylvanus Olympio
950.label: Event
950.description: Independence 1960; Olympio's presidency; assassination 1963 in Africa's first military coup of the independence era; Grunitzky interlude.

950.name: Independence of Togo
950.label: Event
950.description: Togo independent 27 April 1960; Sylvanus Olympio first president; refuses to integrate demobilised soldiers.

950.name: Assassination of Sylvanus Olympio
950.label: Event
950.description: Sergeant Gnassingbé Eyadéma among soldiers who kill Olympio in coup 13 January 1963; Grunitzky installed as president.

950.name: Gnassingbé Eyadéma Dynasty
950.label: Event
950.description: Eyadéma rules Togo for 38 years—one of Africa's longest-serving leaders; RPT single party; cult of personality; democratic façade.

950.name: Eyadéma's Single-Party Rule
950.label: Event
950.description: RPT as sole party; northern Kabye military dominance; cult of personality; phosphate economy.

950.name: Democratic Struggle and 1991 National Conference
950.label: Event
950.description: Pro-democracy movement; Sovereign National Conference 1991; Eyadéma uses military to claw back power; democratic transition fails.

960.name: Faure Gnassingbé and Contemporary Togo
960.label: Event
960.description: Faure Gnassingbé succeeds father in disputed succession; Gnassingbé family becomes Africa's longest ruling dynasty; protests; constitutional changes.

960.name: Faure Gnassingbé's Disputed Succession
960.label: Event
960.description: Military installs Faure Gnassingbé immediately after Eyadéma's death; forced to hold elections; wins amid violence and fraud (~500 killed).

960.name: Gnassingbé Consolidation of Power
960.label: Event
960.description: Faure re-elected 2010, 2015; limited reforms; opposition fragmented; EU re-engagement and sanctions cycles.
